'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Authorities reveal that the attackers who attempted to assassinate [[Uganda]]n general [[Katumba Wamala]] in [[Kampala]] were [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremists]] who were trained in a [[jihadism|jihadist]] camp in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of Congo]], and had links with the [[Allied Democratic Forces]] and the [[Islamic State]]. Wamala was injured during the attack but survived, while his daughter and his driver were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/uganda-links-islamist-rebels-attempted-murder-minister-2021-07-01/ (Reuters)]
**U.S. [[Ambassador]] to the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] [[Michael A. Hammer]] announces that the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] will assist in training [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese forces]] and with [[Military intelligence|intelligence]] sharing. [https://www.newsweek.com/us-sending-soldiers-congo-train-army-help-find-rebels-who-killed-9-attack-1606072 (''Newsweek'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2021 Canadian Indian residential schools gravesite discoveries]]
**[[Indigenous peoples in Canada|Indigenous]] protesters tear down the ''[[Statue of Queen Victoria (Winnipeg)|Statue of Queen Victoria]]'' in [[Winnipeg]], [[Manitoba]], [[Canada]], as protests grow over the [[mass graves]] of indigenous children discovered at former [[Canadian Indian residential school system|Canadian Indian residential schools]]. A smaller statue of [[Monarchy of the United Kingdom|Queen]] [[Elizabeth II]] was also toppled nearby. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-57693683 (BBC News)] Multiple Catholic Churches on or near indigenous grounds have been burned down. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/morinville-church-alberta-burned-fire-1.6085688 (CBC)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of El Salvador]]
**[[President of El Salvador|President]] [[Nayib Bukele]] requests a [[minimum wage]] increase of 20% due to poor [[Salvadorans]] suffering from an "onslaught of global [[inflation]]". Bukele also orders more food handouts to combat hunger during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in El Salvador|ongoing COVID-19 pandemic]]. The country recently had a government reshuffle, which has put in doubt negotiations for a potential $1 billion financing program from the [[International Monetary Fund]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/el-salvadors-bukele-seeks-20-minimum-wage-hike-orders-food-handouts-2021-07-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Economy of Uganda]]
**Uganda imposes a new tax rate for using the [[internet]] as the [[government of Uganda|government]] orders a 12% [[excise duty]] on [[mobile data]]. [[President of Uganda|President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] defends the tax as he says that social media users are "endlessly donating money to foreign telephone companies through chatting or even lying" and described the use of [[social media]] as a "luxury". This tax proposal, which takes effect immediately, resulted in protests in 2018 and 2019. [https://africafeeds.com/2021/07/01/ugandans-paying-new-tax-for-using-the-internet/ (''Africa Feeds'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of China]]
**[[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party|CCP General Secretary]] [[Xi Jinping]] delivered a speech in which he specifically announced the realization of the first goal of the [[Two Centenaries]] goal set. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/06/30/world/china-communist-party-anniversary (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Madagascar food crisis]]
**UN agencies report that due to the [[food insecurity]] that has affected around one million people in [[Madagascar]], the population has been surviving by eating ashes mixed with [[tamarind]] and shoe leather, as the United States and [[South Korea]] pledge [[economic aid]] to [[Malagasy President]] [[Andry Rajoelina]]. [https://metro.co.uk/2021/07/01/starving-people-in-madagascar-eating-ash-during-worst-drought-in-decades-14858844/ (''Metro UK'')]
*[[2021 Western North America heat wave]]
**[[Lytton wildfire]]
***The village of [[Lytton, British Columbia]], is evacuated after a [[wildfire]] destroys 90% of the village amid an unprecedented [[heat wave]] caused by a rare "heat dome" event over the [[Pacific Northwest]] and [[Western Canada]]. The village recently recorded Canada's highest ever temperature of {{convert|49.6|C|F}}. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-57678054 (BBC News)]
*[[2020–2021 Taal Volcano eruptions]]
**The [[Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology]] (PHIVOLCS) raises the alert status of [[Taal Volcano]] to level 3 after the volcano emitted a kilometer-high ash plume, forcing authorities in the [[Provinces of the Philippines|provinces]] of [[Batangas]] and [[Cavite]] to evacuate thousands of people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/1/evacuation-under-way-as-philippines-raises-volcano-danger-level (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] imposes a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] that suspends all [[public transport]] and only allows people to leave their house for emergency reasons due to a substantial increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [[Bangladesh Army|Soldiers]] are deployed to enforce the lockdown. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/bangladesh-lock-down-covid-19-cases-surge (Voice of America)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement]]
*****[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] announces emergency community restrictions in 122 regencies and cities in [[Java]] and [[Bali]], including the capital [[Jakarta]] from July 3 to 20 which would require non-essential businesses and [[Place of worship|places of worship]] to close. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-emergency-covid-19-curbs-be-effective-july-2-20-minister-2021-07-01/ (Reuters)] [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/indonesia-covid-19-emergency-restrictions-ppkm-java-bali-15115348 (CNA)]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 24,836 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.2 million. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5627352/24836-kasus-baru-hari-ini-rekor-tertinggi-sepanjang-sejarah-corona-ri (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 57 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,080. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2141591/record-57-covid-deaths-5-533-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 672 deaths from COVID-19, bringing the nationwide death toll to 135,886. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/07/01/russia-posts-record-covid-deaths-for-third-day-running-a74385 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] lifts nearly all COVID-19-related business restrictions, as well as nighttime and Sunday curfews as the number of cases remains steady. Only [[hookah]] shops continue to remain closed. [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-europe-turkey-pandemics-lifestyle-b95a3b1c535f6d2d413dbdf147208e72 (AP)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Turkey]]
*****[[Turkey]] begins to give a third dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to [[healthcare worker]]s and people aged above 50 years old. [https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-starts-giving-third-dose-of-covid-19-vaccine-165950 (''Hurriyet Daily News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 27,989 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of cases since January 25. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-07-01/uk-records-27989-covid-cases-highest-since-january-25-and-fourth-day-in-a-row-of-more-than-20000-positive-tests (ITV News)]
***The [[European Union]] launches the [[Immunity passport|EU Digital COVID Certificate]] that contains a proof of vaccination, a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]], or proof of recovery from COVID-19, and is designed to allow Europeans to resume travel across the bloc without [[quarantine]] in order to boost tourism. [https://www.ft.com/content/7d48a006-cdfa-4b27-a663-21428471fbc5 (''Financial Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record of 431 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 4,849. The [[Ministry of Health and Medical Services (Fiji)|Ministry of Health and Medical Services]] also reports two deaths, bringing the death toll to 24, with 22 of these deaths having occurred since the current outbreak began in April. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445969/fiji-covid-19-431-new-cases-and-two-deaths (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] announces a month-long vaccination raffle in which residents can win a total of $5 million in cash (one grand prize of $2 million or three prizes of $1 million) and $500,000 total in college scholarships for children aged 12 to 17 years old (nine prizes of $55,000). The winners will be drawn on August 4. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2021/07/nearly-500k-residents-have-signed-up-for-michigans-vaccine-lottery.html (MLive.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sierra Leone]]
***[[President of Sierra Leone|President]] [[Julius Maada Bio]] announces a nationwide curfew in [[Sierra Leone|the country]] to combat the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.thesierraleonetelegraph.com/president-bio-announces-new-measures-to-curb-rising-covid-cases-and-deaths-in-sierra-leone/ (''The Sierra Leone Telegraph'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Turkey–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] adds [[Turkey]] to its list of governments that are implicated in the use of [[child soldier]]s, saying that the country has provided "tangible support" to the [[Neo-Ottomanism|Neo-Ottoman]] [[Sultan Murad Division]], in [[Syria]] and [[Libya]], which uses child soldiers. It is the first time that a [[NATO]] member state has been included in the [[Trafficking in Persons Report]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-adds-turkey-list-countries-implicated-use-child-soldiers-2021-07-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Cannabis in Rwanda]]
**[[Rwanda]] legalizes the [[Medical cannabis|medical use of cannabis]]. However, recreational use of [[cannabis]] remains illegal. [https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/tea/news/east-africa/rwanda-legalises-medical-use-of-cannabis--3456728 (''The East African'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Climate change in Antarctica]]
**The [[United Nations]]' [[World Meteorological Organization]] confirms that a record high temperature of 18.3 °C (64.9 °F) has been recorded in [[Antarctica]] at the [[Esperanza Base]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210701-un-confirms-18-3c-record-heat-in-antarctica (France 24)]
